Spot premium quotations for imported cathode remained subdued over the past two weeks as the significant negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME persisted. Traders reported that the latest spot premium quotations for imported cathode were in a US$30-70/t range, with major traders offering cathode at around $50/t, whereas spot premium quotations for SXEW cathode were quoted at between US$30/t and $50/t. There were very few deals closed, reflecting the lack of physical demand for imported cathode. Some market insiders expect that the © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **March 2012** www.crugroup.com SHFE/LME arbitrage window may not re-open soon, as it is difficult to find signs at the moment that demand will recover in the near future. At the same time, domestic cathode supply is abundant and cathode inventory in SHFE and bonded warehouse remains at a high level. We were told by market participants that cathode inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses currently amount to 450,0

00t-470,000t, which was a rise of 80-90,000t over the past two weeks and is  attributed to traders attempting to avoid incurring losses through the sale of imported metal on the spot market at the current low prices.  We expect inventories of bonded materials may continue to increase as the negative SHFE/LME arbitrage persists.  Some market insiders expect that it may rise towards 600,000t by the end of March. 

# **Demand may not recover much in the short term** 

We mentioned in the previous report that we expect domestic demand to recover in April as seasonally strong consumption begins to be felt in the market.  However we are concerned that it may not come true based on our most recent research on China’s refined copper demand.  We have noticed that all kinds of semis producers’ facility utilisation rates have declined by varying degrees m-o-m and y-o-y, from 2% to 18%.  We believe that it was far-fetched to attribute this solely to the impact of China’s Lunar New Year.  Consumers report that demand usually begins to recover after the Lantern Festival, which was on 6<sup>th</sup> February.  This year, though, it is different as demand still remains weak at the moment.  At the same time they report that it is difficult to find signals that demand will improve in the short term. 

We were told by wire and cable producers that the economic slowdown in 2011 began to affect their operations.  The rates of growth in China’s GDP and IP slowed in 2011 and are expected to decline further in 2012, which should impact the wire and cable industry gradually. Moreover, some market insiders believe that the State Grid investment increase in 2012 will mainly be on inter-regional electricity transmission and transformation.  Copper cable is mainly used in the urban power grid, property development and industrial expansions.  Therefore its demand will not benefit very much.  It is reported that State Grid’s power grid investment in 2011 was RMB301.9B and its power grid investment in 2012 is expected to be RMB309.7B, up 3% y-o-y. In addition, building wire demand was subdued, as it was affected by the severe macro controls applied to the property market.  One large sized wire and cable producer reported that its capacity utilisation is about 60% at the moment, compared to running at full capacity last year. The difficulty it faces currently is that it is short of new orders, which are only one third the level of the same period last year. 

The air conditioner producers say that a high level of final product inventory continues to be a challenge.  It is reported that air conditioner industry inventories are 1-1.5 times the normal level.  We understand that domestic home appliance demand is also very weak currently, attributed to the stimulus policy withdrawal, which brought forward demand during 2009 to

This is a situation that is not expected to change in the short term, as the severe macro control of the property market will continue. We were told by one of the top three Chinese air conditioner producers that the weak demand is leading to a build up in inventories of their products. However, we heard reports that China’s Commercial Ministry may introduce an energy-saving appliances subsidy policy in the near future, which should boost domestic demand, but we do not have a specific schedule yet. Furthermore, refined copper demand in autos and electronics remains weak as well. Overall, at the moment we tend to believe refined copper demand will struggle to recover in the usually robust seasonal way in April. We will follow Chinese copper market developments closely in March to confirm or deny this view. # **Copper prices flat** SHFE 3-month price

The LME 3-month copper price rose back towards $8,700/t on 29th February, driven by the monetary easing in Europe. Moreover, China’s manufacturing improved for a third straight month in February, which supported the copper price as well. The purchasing managers’ index rose to 51.0, the highest since September, from 50.5 in January, based on China’s statistics bureau and logistics federation data. However, according to the latest report, SHFE cathode inventories increased to 221,487t, up by 4,345t compared to 14 days ago. In response, the SHFE 3-month copper price fluctuated between RMB59,090-60,460/t during the past two weeks. At the same time, the Shanghai physical price remained below the SHFE cash-month price, which indicates weak demand for physical copper units. Consumers are reluctant to purchase copper as they are short of new orders and credit remains tight. China’s Central Bank did cut the reserve ratio effective from 24th February. We understand that the reduction will not © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 4 **March 2012** www.crugroup.com significantly lift credit constraints, although further easing measures are expected by market insiders. National People’s Congress and Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference will be held over the coming two weeks. We will have to await the end of the congress to see where economic policy is headed and how this may affect copper demand. In the short term we tend to be

lieve the high level of the copper price will not be sustainable from the fundamental point of view.  However, the high level of cancelled warrants in the USA and improved investor sentiment are likely to support the copper price.  We forecast the SHFE 3-month copper price will trade between RMB58,000-60,000/t during the next two weeks.
